postprocess.reason: Remediation of the C5-02 audit (audits/AUDIT_cycle5_c5_02_gpt62_astra.md): the raw measurements of the source result are unchanged; analysis, derived and caveats are recomputed with the corrected token-exposure statement, the corrected split-access and pilot chronology, the unique and inherited hardware counts and the tightened caveats, and the result is checked by the hardened validator. Nothing was retrained.

analysis.sign_convention: every difference is x - y of the contrast (arm_x with method_x minus arm_y with method_y); a negative delta_nll_diff means that x loses less quality under PTQ, a negative nll_diff that its quantized NLL is lower
analysis.inference_note: p_two_sided is the exact df = 4 Student-t p-value of the paired differences; p_sign_flip is the exact two-sided sign-flip permutation p-value over the 2^5 sign patterns (it cannot be below 0.0625, so it never passes a Holm correction over more than one cell). p_holm: Holm-Bonferroni over the cells of one family ('primary' or 'own_best') of one contrast, split and endpoint; p_holm_across_contrasts: over that family of all contrasts; p_holm_all_cells: over every cell of one contrast.
analysis.primary_note: The families cover the (format, mode) cells with more than one method. 'primary': arm contrasts use the base method with the lowest val NLL pooled over all arms and seeds for both sides; AWQ contrasts compare the val-selected AWQ method (pooled over the AWQ arms) with that base method. 'own_best': each side uses the method with the lowest val NLL of its own arm (AWQ contrasts: the arm's best AWQ method against the other arm's best base method), i.e. the best deployable result of each side. 'cells' of an AWQ contrast compare each AWQ method with the same rotation without scaling (alpha = 0).

caveats: Five paired seeds give 4 degrees of freedom. The seeds share one corpus, one calibration draw and one set of test documents; the intervals condition on these and on the val-selected methods, and they omit the variation of new documents, of a new calibration draw and of a repeated method selection. The Student-t p-values and 95% intervals assume normal paired differences (df = 4). Holm-Bonferroni is applied to the paired-t p-values over the 6 cells of one family of one contrast (p_holm) and over the 48 cells of that family across the 8 contrasts (p_holm_across_contrasts). The exact two-sided sign-flip p-value cannot be below 0.0625, so it cannot pass a 0.05 threshold, with or without a correction. Absence of significance is not evidence of equal PTQ sensitivity. Inference is restricted to the 50m preset in this training regime on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (sm_120).

AdamW is one run per seed, stopped on val.bin, and the selected step's weights (preceding the stopping step on seeds 3 and 4) are evaluated without retraining. The val match of Stage B is therefore the Stage A match by construction. test.bin is held out from the canonical selection rules: training, stopping, checkpoint selection, calibration, alpha selection and method selection read train.bin and val.bin only. It is not a previously unseen study-level holdout: seed-0 shakedown runs (timing_seed0.log and timing_seed0b.log; shakedown JSON SHA-256 39f2d27e...) scored the same test.bin before the initial commit 05ea4ae and the amendment 0355d16, and the logs cannot show whether a person used those scores for a design decision. Training is not bit-reproducible on this host: fresh AdamW runs of one configuration differed by 0.06 to 0.07 nats on val.bin in the design pilot, so a retrain gives other weights and another stopping step.

Iso-loss is not iso-compute and not iso-schedule: AdamW draws more training tokens than Muon (adamw_over_muon_tokens per seed) and ends with a seed-dependent number of floor-LR steps (adamw_floor_lr_steps), while Muon ends when its cosine reaches the floor. Validation stopping, the additional token exposure, the floor-LR phase and the fresh restart are coupled in this recipe, and the experiment has no fixed-step or fixed-exposure control. It cannot isolate which of them causes the mean BF16 test gap of +0.0037 nats (Muon minus AdamW). The selection conditions the val gap on its target. The result is for this recipe; it supports no optimizer-wide PTQ ratio claim.

The AdamW cosine length and the first measured step come from a seed-0 design pilot. The AdamW step cap was raised from 1280 to 2560 after the first canonical attempt (commit 05ea4ae) was stopped in Stage A: seed 1 had matched at step 640, and the AdamW run of seed 2 was 0.58 nats above Muon at step 400 and still 0.0925 nats above it at step 1280, where its log ends. That attempt has no Stage B scores; its startup verification read test.bin (hashes and document boundaries) and scored no model. The canonical run of the amended commit 0355d16 trained fresh trajectories, and every one stopped below step 1280. The pilot floor-LR probe is a sensitivity check at different losses, not an equal-loss proof: identity-GPTQ val NLL increase 0.0010 (NVFP4) / 0.0096 (INT2 g16) at val NLL 5.414 of a run stopped at 848 steps, against 0.0010 / 0.0106 at 5.298 and 0.0008 / 0.0106 at 5.235 for fresh cosine runs of 544 and 608 steps (val NLL 5.235-5.414). In the canonical five-seed run, the primary AdamW test delta-NLL means at LR 0.001 are 1.38-4.02x those of the C4-01b AdamW recipe at LR 0.0015 (NVFP4 W4A16 2.60x, dynamic W4A4 1.42x, static W4A4 1.38x, MXFP4 1.97x, INT2 g16 3.54x, INT2 g32 4.02x); seeds, stopping, duration and LR changed together, so the difference is not attributed to the LR.

Both cooldown arms branch from snapshots of the seed's Muon run, so their first 256 / 272 steps are that run's steps. Their BF16 baselines differ from Muon; bf16_nll_diff and nll_diff report the net effect. The QAT cooldown targets identity-coordinate nvfp4_g16 round-to-nearest only; GPTQ and the rotations change the rounded values or the coordinates, so the arm is a test of that one target, not of QAT in general. The AdamW cooldown is an optimizer switch. No explicit spectral penalty was tested; stable rank and alignment are measured, not varied independently.

The alpha of the activation-aware scaling is selected per checkpoint, format and rotation on val.bin with weight-only fake quantization; the hardware W4A4 rows reuse that alpha. The weight-only selection is a proxy: only the selected alpha and the unscaled row are scored on hardware, so the selection can miss the alpha that is best under hardware W4A4. The AWQ results hold for this selection rule; they do not show that a W4A4-tuned scaling is ineffective.

One 50m model family, one calibration draw and short training. Training batches are BatchStream draws with replacement: every optimizer step takes 64 independent 513-token slices at uniform random starts (no sequential cursor), so exposure is given in training-set token equivalents (tokens drawn / 26,004,518 tokens of train.bin), not in epochs of distinct tokens. Muon and both cooldown arms draw 0.403 token equivalents (320 steps). The selected AdamW checkpoints are at steps 672-944, 0.847-1.190 token equivalents; the selected checkpoints of seeds 2 and 3 are above one token equivalent (1.190 and 1.109). The AdamW runs actually trained 672-944 steps, 0.847-1.190 token equivalents: seed 3 trained 896 steps = 1.129 token equivalents before the selection of step 880 = 1.109 and seed 4 trained 800 steps = 1.008 token equivalents before the selection of step 784 = 0.988. A compute comparison must count every step actually run. More exposure both repeats and adds training positions and can change generalization and geometry; there is no fixed-step or fixed-exposure control. PTQ sensitivity of longer-trained or larger models can differ.

Hessians come from one forward pass of the full-precision model (parallel GPTQ). Static activation scales are calibrated on the BF16 model. Dynamic W4A4 scales are per forward batch (16 x 512 tokens).

Layer-geometry p-values are descriptive and not corrected for multiplicity. Rows with alpha = 0 are copies of their unscaled twin rows, not new measurements: 20 of the 200 hardware W4A4 rows and 600 of the 6000 matrix decode comparisons are inherited (analysis.hardware gives the unique and the inherited counts).
